title: Integrated security & compliance guidance: RBAC, audit logging, data residency, SDLC, incident response, evidence & exceptions
author: Aria Patel
content:
Summary
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's baseline requirements and operational procedures for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident-response security procedures, audit evidence workflows, and the process for risk exceptions. It is intended for security engineers, platform owners, product managers, and compliance owners who need a single reference for implementing and verifying controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to all Redwood-managed control planes and hosted services, plus standard guidance for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Customer-specific requirements that are stricter than the guidance (e.g., contractual SLAs, region-only residency commitments) take precedence.
- This document does not replace team-level runbooks; it defines minimums and workflows for company-wide controls.

1) RBAC and authentication
Overview
We use a least-privilege RBAC model across Redwood services and admin consoles. Role definitions are centrally versioned, documented, and enforced in the identity provider and the platform control plane.
Minimum roles and responsibilities
- Organization roles: super-admin (security/ops), org-admin (customer onboarding), billing-admin (finance), audit-reader (compliance), infra-operator (SRE/infra), developer (prod deploy), support (customer support scoped).
- Resource-level roles: project-owner, project-developer, model-deployer, read-only-observer.
- Service principals: short-lived service identities for automated processes (CI/CD, backup jobs).
Authentication requirements
1. All human users must authenticate via SSO (OIDC/SAML) where available.
2. 2FA (TOTP or U2F security keys) required for org-admin, super-admin, and any user with write access to production infrastructure.
3. Service principals must use short-lived tokens (max validity 24 hours) and rotate credentials automatically.
4. API keys for customers are scoped to product routes and support rotation. Long-lived secrets are forbidden unless approved and reviewed by security.
Enforcement and provisioning
- IdP (Okta) integration: groups map to platform roles via SCIM. Role mapping changes require an approval event logged in the change-management system.
- Provisioning workflow: owner requests -> manager approval -> security review for elevated roles -> SCIM sync.
- Access reviews: quarterly automated access-review emails to owners with a one-click revoke option.
Audit and telemetry
- Every role grant/revoke, privilege elevation, and SSO failure must be logged (see Audit Logging section).
- SLO: role-execution events should appear in the SIEM within 5 minutes, 95% of the time.

2) Audit logging
What we log (minimum)
- Authentication events: successful and failed login attempts, MFA challenges, token issuance and revocation.
- Authorization decisions: grants, revokes, policy evaluations, and resource-level ACL changes.
- Administrative activity: role changes, onboarding/offboarding, IAM policy updates, enterprise config changes.
- Data access: reads and writes to customer data stores that could be subject to compliance review (include requestor, timestamp, resource, operation, request ID).
- Runtime events: model-serving configuration changes, deployment rollouts, autoscaling actions, and fallback events.
Logging format and transport
- All audit events are JSON objects with a canonical schema: timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success/failure), request_id, source_ip, user_agent, and metadata (stringified).
- Events are forwarded to the central logging ingestion cluster (Kafka) and then to the SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) with TLS and mutual auth.
- Retention policy is applied at the SIEM tier; raw compressed logs are archived to cold storage for long-term retention.
Retention and retention exceptions
- Default retention: 2 years for operational audit logs; 7 years for logs related to financial or legal obligations.
- For regulated customers with residency commitments, logs may be retained in-region per contract (see Data Residency section).
- Exceptions to retention limits require documented business justification and signoff by InfoSec and Legal.
Alerting and monitoring
- Create correlation rules for: repeated failed auth attempts (>= 5 / 10 min), privilege escalation without approval, and large-volume data exports by a single principal.
- Incident threshold definitions: medium (1–5 suspicious auth events), high (>5 or confirmed exfiltration).

3) Data residency and retention
Residency model
- Redwood maintains regional data partitions: us-west, us-east, eu-west, apac. Customers may select a primary residency for customer data and audit artifacts at purchase/contract.
- Control-plane metadata (non-sensitive telemetry) is logically separated and does not by default include customer data unless specifically required.
Retention schedules (default)
- Customer customer-data (per-tenant application data): retention per customer SLA; default 1 year unless contractual change.
- Audit logs: 2 years (default); 7 years for financial/legal required artifacts.
- Backups: full backups retained 90 days in hot storage; encrypted cold backups retained 2 years unless the customer requests deletion earlier.
Data deletion workflow
1. Customer initiates deletion via Console or API -> ticket opened in customer-ops.
2. Customer-ops verifies identity and entitlement -> creates deletion job with request_id.
3. Deletion job executes: remove live data, purge backups per backup-policy, remove indexed artifacts, and mark the tenant as deleted in internal catalog.
4. Audit entry created with deletion result and retention of the deletion evidence artifact for 1 year.
Cross-border transfers and legal holds
- Cross-border transfers are allowed only when contractually permitted. Legal holds override deletion workflows and are processed by Legal + Security with documented scope and end-date.

4) Secure SDLC (development and release controls)
Policy overview
All code changes that reach production must pass automated quality and security gates and follow the release governance below.
Required controls
- Code review: at least one peer review for non-trivial changes; two reviewers for security-sensitive subsystems (auth, billing, infra).
- CI gates: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis (linting), SAST, dependency vulnerability scanning, secret-scan.
- Dependency management: denylist high-risk packages; require CVE-free status or documented mitigations for any dependency with critical severity older than 72 hours.
- Secrets: no secrets in git; use the vault service (HashiCorp Vault/Secrets Manager). Commit hooks and scanning enforced in CI.
- Build artifacts: builds must be reproducible and signed. Release artifacts stored in the artifact registry with immutable tags.
Release controls and rollout
- Canary rollout policy: 5% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor errors and latency, then 25% for 30 minutes, then 100% if no regressions.
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rate > 2% over baseline for 10 minutes, or P50 latency degradation > 30%.
- Production access: only infra-operator and approved SRE runbooks may perform emergency hotfixes; all hotfixes must be post-hoc reviewed within 24 hours.
Supply chain and third-party verification
- Vendor risk assessments required for any third-party dependency that handles customer data.
- SBOMs generated for all production images and kept with release metadata for audit purposes.

5) Incident response - security procedures
Goals
- Detect, contain, eradicate, recover, and preserve evidence while meeting breach notification obligations.
Call tree and ownership
- Triage lead: oncall security engineer -> incident commander (IC) -> post-incident review owner (PIO).
- Communication channels: PagerDuty -> dedicated incident Slack channel (#incident-<id>) -> incident bridge.
Detection and triage
1. Triage receives alert (SIEM, monitoring, or external report).
2. Determine impact scope: affected tenants, systems, data classification.
3. Classify incident severity (low/medium/high/critical) using predefined criteria (e.g., confirmed data exfiltration => critical).
Containment and forensics
- Imaging: preserve volatile evidence (memory images) for suspicious host compromises.
- Network: apply temporary blocking rules, WAF signatures, or route to mitigations to stop ongoing exfiltration.
- Evidence preservation: snapshot logs, preserve request-ids, export SIEM events, and disable log rotation for impacted buckets. Maintain chain-of-custody notes.
Notification and legal obligations
- Internal: execs and legal informed within 2 hours for high/critical incidents.
- Customer notification: within contractual/legally-required windows (72 hours for GDPR breach notification where required). Follow the customer notification template stored in the incident repository.
Recovery and root cause
- Recovery steps executed by infra/SRE with the security lead validating eradication.
- Post-incident: timeline, root cause, remediation plan, and validation steps published within 7 business days.
Postmortem and remediation tracking
- Postmortems are required for severity >= medium. Action items tracked in the remediation board and assigned owners with due dates.

6) Compliance evidence workflows (audits and requests)
Evidence catalog and owners
- Evidence types: access logs, role change records, change approvals, SAML/OIDC configuration snapshots, vulnerability scan reports, SBOMs, runbook copies, data deletion proof, and encryption key rotation logs.
- Each evidence artifact must include: artifact_id, generation_date, owner, retention_period, storage_location, and hash (or signed metadata).
Automated evidence collection
- Quarterly audit pack: automatically collect the previous quarter's configuration snapshots, role-change exports, and signed SBOMs. Pack is staged to the evidence store for reviewers.
- On-demand evidence requests: compliance portal ticket triggers a workflow that pulls relevant artifacts and stamps them with request_id and reviewer.
Evidence review and signoff
- Reviewer from Legal/Compliance reviews artifacts and records a signoff entry. Manual attestations (e.g., interviews) are recorded as meeting notes and linked to the artifact.
Proof of deletion and retention proof
- Deletion evidence includes the deletion request, job execution trace, confirmation of backup purge steps, and a verification scan that the tenant id no longer appears in indexes.
Audit timeline SLOs
- Internal requests: evidence delivered to reviewer within 48 business hours.
- External (certification) audits: audit pack delivered within agreed contract timeframes (typically 5–10 business days).

7) Risk and exceptions process
When to request an exception
- Exceptions are requested when strict adherence to a control prevents delivery of a critical business need and a compensating control can be applied.
Request process
1. Exception request submitted via the risk-exceptions portal with: owner, scope, systems affected, duration, compensating controls, and risk mitigation plan.
2. Security performs a risk assessment and assigns risk scoring (impact x likelihood).
3. Approval matrix: low-risk exceptions approved by Security Manager; medium-risk require Legal + Security Director; high-risk require CTO and CISO signoff.
4. Timebox: exceptions are time-limited (max 90 days) and must include monitoring requirements.
Monitoring and re-evaluation
- Exception owner must provide weekly status updates and a final remediation plan prior to expiry. Exceptions automatically escalate one week before expiry.
Tracking and auditability
- All exceptions stored in the risk register with approvals, compensating controls, and links to related evidence. Exceptions are included in quarterly risk reviews.

Appendices
A. Canonical audit event example (JSON)
{
  "timestamp": "2027-03-04T15:12:34Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_123",
  "actor_id": "user:aria.patel@redwood.com",
  "actor_type": "human",
  "action": "role_grant",
  "resource_type": "organization:project",
  "resource_id": "proj_456",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-9a8b7c",
  "source_ip": "18.25.33.100",
  "user_agent": "OKTA-SSO/1.2",
  "metadata": "{\"reason\":\"onboarding\"}"
}

B. Evidence checklist (example)
- Role grants export for time window (CSV)
- Audit log slice for request IDs
- SAML metadata snapshot
- Signed SBOM for active images
- Vulnerability scan results and remediation tickets
- Deletion job traces (if relevant)
